### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a00b42287669b261ae1c9fd9a42059bf87c91953`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a00b42287669b261ae1c9fd9a42059bf87c91953` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5018544683e98f056537a1457ed5ff0454b87528` — the merge of head `b8cd61943af04da53e3c3645e77eb28d90b2616e` into base `a00b42287669b261ae1c9fd9a42059bf87c91953`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5018544683e98f056537a1457ed5ff0454b87528 && git checkout 5018544683e98f056537a1457ed5ff0454b87528
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a00b42287669b261ae1c9fd9a42059bf87c91953 b8cd61943af04da53e3c3645e77eb28d90b2616e && git checkout -B drift-repro a00b42287669b261ae1c9fd9a42059bf87c91953 && git merge --no-ff b8cd61943af04da53e3c3645e77eb28d90b2616e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a00b42287669b261ae1c9fd9a42059bf87c91953
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a00b42287669b261ae1c9fd9a42059bf87c91953` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dbb037a8603a91ad571a0b3a3a4b64c4a3505c93`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx, .changeset/34275-blueprint-field-multiple-accept-maxsize.md

Read at 2026-11-16T04:35Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6907368086; lane request 6907342312 on mailbox #33873. Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:spec#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

First review of this PR: there are no prior finding ids to continue. Read outside the diff, never reviewed: `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/default-value-shape.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/stage-field-kinds.ts`, and `FieldSchema`'s refinement in `field.zod.ts` at this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Value shapes (holds).** Read against `FieldSchema` at this head: `accept` is `z.array(z.string()).optional()` and `maxSize` is `z.number().int().positive().optional()` on both; the strict mirror swaps `.optional()` for `.nullable()`. `multiple` is `z.boolean()` on both, without `FieldSchema`'s `.default(false)` on the blueprint side, so a field that omits it gains no key. Units (bytes) and the media family (`FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES`: image, file, avatar, video, audio) are stated as `FieldSchema` states them. The 23-value battery pins each lenient and strict leaf against `FieldSchema.shape[key]`.
- **Cross-key parity for `accept` / `maxSize` (holds).** `FieldSchema`'s refinement carries no rule on either key (no refusal outside the media family), so the blueprint refusing nothing there is parity, as the card asks. The describes say "on any other type it parses and nothing reads it", which is true of the schema.
- **Cross-key parity for `multiple` at the key (holds).** `refuseUndeclarableMultiple` reads the same set function as `FieldSchema` and the same radio carve-out; the per-`FieldType` pin compares the two refusals at the `multiple` path type by type. `multiple: false` is never refused.
- **Cross-key parity for `multiple` beyond the key (does NOT hold, see M1).** `FieldSchema` has three rules that read `multiple` on a `select`: the default (covered by this PR), the stage field (covered, because `refuseStageFieldWithoutKinds` is the shared function and reads `multiple` on the entry; the blueprint field now carries the key into it), and option `kind` (not covered).
- **Point 1, the export (holds).** The diff to `field.zod.ts` is the `export` keyword, the rename at the definition and at its two callers, and the docblock. The body is the same expression over the same two sets, and no reference to the old name remains at this head, so `FieldSchema` and the remedy list read the identical memoised set and every `FieldSchema` caller sees the same refusal. A function, not a constant, is forced by the load-order note in its own docblock. The name says what it answers ("may an author declare `multiple` here") and does not collide with `isMultiValueField`. It returns the live set typed read-only, the same pattern as the sibling exported sets. Accepted.
- **Point 2, the added rule (holds, and is the right rule).** On the built field a multi-value `select` judges a literal default against the list contract and refuses every runtime token on a multi-value field, so the only default it can take is an array; the blueprint key is `boolean | number | string` and can carry none. Refusing at `defaultValue`, before the token branch, is therefore correct for literal and token alike. The condition (`multiple === true`, an admitted type, not `radio`, in the declarable set) selects exactly `select`; every other declarable type already takes no blueprint default and keeps its own reason, and `radio` is left to the `multiple` refusal. It reaches only inputs carrying `multiple: true`.
- **Point 3, the carrier (does not overclaim, with one exception in M1).** The describes say "carried into the built field by the applier" and the PR body marks the cloud side NOT MEASURED; no in-repo code outside `packages/spec` parses the lenient schema (one lint test reads its shape). The phrases "which the built field offers to the file picker and checks on write" restate `FieldSchema`'s own describes. The transition window is disclosed.
- **`StrictField` vs `BlueprintFieldSchema` (holds).** Same three keys, same leaves, shared rule text; the strict describes add the null spelling only.
- **Liveness (no row owed).** `packages/spec/liveness/` holds no ledger for the blueprint types; the three keys land in `authorable-surface/ai.json` beside `ai/BlueprintField:defaultValue`, which has none either.
- **Docs page (true to the schema).** Both tables in `solution-blueprint.mdx` carry the three rows and the amended `defaultValue` sentence, matching the describes.
- **Skills-docs (reason holds).** `skills/**` names the module in one pointer row of `skills/objectstack-ai/references/_index.md` and teaches no blueprint field key.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `minor` is correct: `Metadata-protocol: added` takes at least minor, and the new `data` export (`multiDeclarableFieldTypes (function)` in `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json`, origin `src/data/field.zod.ts`) is additive. The three `ai/BlueprintField:*` rows in `authorable-surface/ai.json` match `added`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds at the door the card measured; see S1 for the one sentence the changeset owes about a direct parse.

CI on this head: 67 check-runs, 56 success, 10 skipped, 1 still running (`Test Core (8/8)`), none failed. This record is a FAIL on M1 regardless of how that run ends.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `FieldSchema` behaviour change: the refinement body is untouched apart from the callee's name.
- No ADR-0087 conversion owed: nothing stored changes meaning, and no key is removed.
- Cross-repo: cloud#4400 carries the keys; the pin bump and the applier's allow-list should land together, as the PR body says. Not measured here.
- Nothing security-touching was found in this diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**M1 (must-fix) — a multi-value `select` whose options declare `kind` parses on the blueprint and is refused by the built field.** `FieldSchema` (#23809) refuses an option `kind` on any field that is not a single-value `select` / `radio`, one issue per option at `options.N.kind`, and names `multiple: true` in the message. The blueprint field admits `options[].kind` and, with this PR, `multiple: true` on a `select`, and no rule joins them. So `{ type: 'select', multiple: true, options: [{ label, value, kind: 'open' }] }` is a combination this PR newly admits, that parses here, and that the object write refuses. It is the same hole the PR closed for `defaultValue` ("without this branch the widening opened a hole"), left open one key over, and three texts say it does not exist: the changeset ("the blueprint can propose no `multiple` the built field refuses"), the `refuseUndeclarableMultiple` docblock, and the new `field.zod.ts` docblock ("a blueprint can never propose a declaration the built field refuses"). The parity pin compares refusals at the `multiple` path only, so it cannot see this. Fix: one branch in `refineBlueprintField` refusing `kind` on the options of a `select` with `multiple: true`, by name at the option's `kind`, pinned against `FieldSchema` like the default rule, plus one clause in `MULTIPLE_RULE`. The pre-existing `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` case is taught by the `kind` describe and is not this PR's to change; the three sentences should then claim what is pinned.

**S1 (should-fix) — the changeset's "nothing is removed or narrowed" and "nothing an author wrote before parses differently" are true at the build door, not of a direct parse.** `BlueprintFieldSchema` is a plain `z.object`, which drops an undeclared key. Before this PR a direct `parse` of a field carrying `multiple: true` on a `text`, `maxSize: 0`, or a multi-value `select` with a default succeeded with the key dropped; it is now refused. No author reached that through `apply_blueprint` (the door refuses undeclared keys) and no in-repo code parses the lenient schema outside the spec's tests, so I do not ask for a different declaration; the changeset should say it in one sentence so a direct caller reads the FROM and TO.

**N1 (nit) — the stage-field path is newly reachable and unpinned.** An object whose `stageField` names a `select` with `multiple: true` is now refused at `stageField` by the shared function. Correct behaviour; one case in the new describe would pin it.

How the delta was read. Four commits sit on dbb037a8: `c45556bf` (the fix), `2f073725` (reference page regenerated), `cc5edaea` (merge of main at a00b4228, 20 commits) and `b8cd6194` (authorable surface regenerated). `git diff dbb037a8 2f073725` is the round's own work: five of the PR's files, +88/-13. Main's 20 commits touch exactly one of the PR's eight files, `authorable-surface/ai.json`, by one row (`ai/Skill:mcpPrompt`), and nothing under `packages/spec/src/data` or the blueprint module. Read outside the diff, never reviewed: `FieldSchema`'s refinement and `ObjectSchema`'s refinement at this head, `packages/spec/src/data/stage-field-kinds.ts`. One correction to the handoff and the dev report, which name `0dbf86fe` as the fix commit: that id is the blob of `solution-blueprint.zod.ts` after the fix; the commit is `c45556bf`.

### ① Derived judgments

Prior findings (record 6907437381):

- **M1 (kind on a multi-value `select`): closed.** `c45556bf` adds `refuseKindOnMultiValueSelect` to `refineBlueprintField`. Read against `FieldSchema`'s #23809 rule at this head: same condition for the case this PR opened (`select` with `multiple: true`), one `custom` issue per option that declares a kind, at `options.N.kind`, the built field's wording with the field named in front. An absent kind is skipped as on `FieldSchema`; a null kind is skipped here and left to the key's own enum issue on the lenient side, and is the strict mirror's spelling of absence. `radio` with `multiple: true` is left to the `multiple` refusal, whose remedy makes the kinds legal, and the docblock says so. The pin parses the same three options through both schemas and compares the refused paths (options 0 and 2, not the kind-less option 1), with controls: the same kinds on a single-value select parse on both, a multi-value select without kinds parses, and the strict mirror's null kinds are not refused. The three texts the prior record named now claim what is pinned: the changeset ("refused on exactly the types the built field refuses it on"), the `refuseUndeclarableMultiple` docblock (which points at the two neighbouring rules, "each pinned against `FieldSchema` on its own"), and the `field.zod.ts` docblock. `MULTIPLE_RULE` carries the clause, on both sides and in both tables of the reference page.
- **S1 (changeset FROM / TO for a direct parse): closed.** The changeset now scopes "nothing an author wrote before parses differently" to the `apply_blueprint` door and states the direct-parse FROM (key dropped) and TO (refused at `multiple`, `maxSize`, `defaultValue`) with three examples, each true of the schema at this head. One residue, N1 below.
- **N1 (stage-field path unpinned): closed.** A new case parses an object whose `stageField` names a `select` with `multiple: true` and expects one issue at `stageField`; the control (the single-value select) shows no issue at `stageField`. The changeset states the behaviour.

Re-derived for this head:

- **Completeness of the cross-key parity (holds).** Every rule in `FieldSchema`'s refinement that reads `multiple` was re-listed at this head: the declarable-set and `radio` refusals (mirrored at the key), the default (mirrored at `defaultValue`), option `kind` (mirrored by this round), and `lookupAutofill`, a key the blueprint field does not declare. `ObjectSchema` reads a field's `multiple` in the stage-field rule (shared function, now pinned) and in `referenceDeletedWhen`, which the blueprint does not declare. No fourth combination the blueprint admits and the built field refuses was found.
- **Merge resolution (clean, no hand edit survives).** `git show --remerge-diff cc5edaea` differs from the mechanical merge in one line: the merge kept the branch's `ai.json` and so dropped main's `ai/Skill:mcpPrompt`; `b8cd6194` regenerates the file and restores it. Net against a00b4228 the three generated files differ by exactly the PR's rows: three `ai/BlueprintField:*` rows, one `multiDeclarableFieldTypes` row in each of `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json`. The PR's file list against the new merge base is the same eight files, +407/-25.
- **Everything the first record marked "holds"** (value shapes, `accept` / `maxSize` parity, the export, the default rule, the carrier wording, strict against lenient, liveness, skills-docs) is untouched by the delta except where named above, and stands.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` `minor` stands: `Metadata-protocol: added`, one additive `data` export, three authorable rows. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` holds at the door the card measured; the direct-parse narrowing is now stated in the changeset body.

CI on this head: 72 check-runs, 60 success, 12 skipped, none running, none failed. The pull request reads mergeable and clean; main has moved one commit past a00b4228, touching none of the eight files.
CI completed before posting: 72 check-runs on this head, 60 success, 12 skipped, none failed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `FieldSchema` behaviour change in the delta: `field.zod.ts` changes one docblock sentence.
- No ADR-0087 conversion owed: nothing stored changes meaning, no key is removed.
- Cross-repo: cloud#4400 carries the keys; pin bump and applier allow-list together, as the PR body says. Not measured here.
- Nothing security-touching was found in the delta or in the merge resolution.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The added rule is the right shape: a third named function in the one refinement, so the dropped-refinements ledger does not move, refusing at the key the author must edit, with the remedy in the message. Leaving the pre-existing `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` kind case alone is correct for this card; the `kind` describe already teaches it.

**N1 (nit, continues S1) — the changeset's `Clause-②` line still ends "Nothing is removed or narrowed." without the door qualifier.** Two paragraphs below it the same file says a direct parse now refuses three inputs it used to accept with the key dropped. The body is right and the declaration stands; the header sentence would read true on its own as "Nothing is removed or narrowed at the `apply_blueprint` door." The direct-parse list could also name the option `kind` case, which the bullet below it covers. No effect on the contract; not blocking.

## 席位核对
